newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-US West treasurer very pleased with deal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-US West treasurer very pleased with deal.

text.p: U.S. West Inc. Treasurer James Anderson, said that he was "very pleased" with the historic $4.1 billion bond offering completed by the company's finance subsidiary on Thursday.

The deal set a record as the largest U.S. investment-grade debt offering in history and tied a high-yield debt deal by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp in 1989 as the largest overall debt offering in history.
Anderson said "tremendous investor demand" allowed the company to increase the size of the offering to $4.1 billion.
It had orginally planned a $2 billion offering.
He confirmed all of the proceeds for the offering will be used to refinance debt assumed during U.S. West's acquisition of Continental Cablevision Inc.

Asked what attracted investors to the deal, he said, "I think investors liked the story very much. The timing was good, we hit the market at the beginning of the year when investors have money to put to work."
"We were happy with spreads over Treasuries," he said adding that the pricing "was attractive to us and obviously attractive to investors," he said.

Anderson said US West sold a $200 million tranch of the deal, added at the last minute, to a single investor which he described as a "major investment fund." The 35-year tranch, callable after 10-years, was priced at 132 basis points over Treasuries.
During the roadshow, company executives said U.S West's cable subsidiary would require $600 million of additional financing to upgrade its cable holdings in 1997.
"We said in our road show that we have public stock of Teleport, worth about $550 million, and Time Warner, worth about $180 million at current market rates. It is possible we could monetize those."

He noted the Justice Department has mandated that US West sell its stake in Teleport by the end of 1998 for anti-trust reasons. US West acquired the Teleport and Time Warner stakes during its acquisition of Continental last year.
He declined to comment on whether the company was currently negotiating to sell the stake to private buyers.
Anderson added the company currently has no plans to issue additional debt.
